Name: complementarity_not_proximity
Title: Complementarity, Not Proximity: What a Reader Keeps of a Foreign Writer's Experience Is Set by the Writer's Solutions to the Reader's Own Failures, Not by Action Agreement, Item Count or Optimality
Short Hypothesis: For success-filtered experience pools collected on the same task set at the same episode budget and serialized in the reader's scaffold, the net gain a reader keeps from a foreign writer's pool over its own matched-cost pool is governed by complementarity, the writer's solutions to the games the reader fails, summarized offline as kappa(W,R) = sum_t share_t * max(0, p_W(t) - p_R(t)); it is not governed by policy proximity (writer-reader action agreement), by the writer's overall success, by item count, or by trajectory optimality. Concretely: at matched per-type item count a foreign pool beats the reader's own pool exactly in the cells where kappa >= 0.08 and not where kappa <= 0.02, including mutual gain between two equally capable backbones with different type profiles; lowering action agreement at fixed capability (same backbone, other temperature or scaffold) moves the gain by less than 0.4 of the Gate-0 effect, while raising capability at the same lowered agreement moves it by more than 0.25; and for one writer at identical item count, its solutions to games the reader fails carry the gain while its optimal solutions to games the reader already solves are worth no more than the reader's own solutions to those same games.
Related Work: Agent Memory Distillation (arXiv:2608.07169) transfers a strong teacher's memory to 4B-8B students and asserts that effectiveness depends on 'teacher capability and student compatibility' without measuring either or comparing against a student-collected pool. Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All (arXiv:2605.30723) and arXiv:2605.23899 show skill utility is backbone-dependent but do not say which property of the writer-reader pair predicts it. Cross-model memory pools (arXiv:2604.14004) and population stores (arXiv:2606.19911) report transfer without manipulating the writer. In imitation learning, DAgger (arXiv:1011.0686) shows that expert labels on the learner's own visited states beat expert demonstrations drawn from the expert's distribution, a training-time, state-level result with one expert; demonstration compatibility between demonstrators is measured for a trained policy (arXiv:2210.08073); retrieval-based behaviour cloning copies the nearest expert action (arXiv:2306.09082, arXiv:2606.09758); recovery-trajectory self-training is argued to beat cloning from experts that never fail (arXiv:2501.11425). None manipulates the demonstrator's identity for an in-context reader, and none separates a demonstrator's solutions to the learner's failures from its optimal solutions to the learner's successes at matched item count. The archived idea closer_beats_stronger (5.75) claimed proximity predicts transfer; judges noted proximity and capability were not separated and there was no self-pool control. This proposal manipulates proximity at fixed capability and capability at fixed proximity, adds the matched-cost self pool, breaks the coverage-count confound by per-type count matching, and predicts the opposite of closer_beats_stronger.
Abstract: Every measured agent-memory gain in this program was written and read by the same policy or by an expert planner, and the 2026 literature moves experience between models without saying what governs how much survives the move. We build a writer x reader design on ALFWorld with writer identity as the manipulated variable: writers X (expert walkthroughs), Q-self (Qwen3-32B, T=0), Q-prox (same backbone, temperature or scaffold changed so that k=0 success is unchanged but action agreement with the reader falls), Q-cap (same backbone with thinking on, thoughts stripped from stored items, k=0 at least 12 points higher, agreement matched to Q-prox), E-self (EXAONE-4.0-32B) and G-self (gpt-oss-120b), each collected once on the same 3,553 training games and success-filtered; readers Q and E. Two statistics are computed offline before any transfer cell: proximity pi(W,R), the reader's greedy-action agreement with the writer's stored actions on 300 states, and complementarity kappa(W,R) = sum_t share_t * max(0, p_W(t) - p_R(t)), the writer's per-type success advantage where the reader fails. Bank construction is uniform: every foreign pool is subsampled per task type to the reader's own success count, so it carries the reader's own type histogram and differs only in who wrote the items and on which games; the reader's own matched-cost pool is the denominator of the retained-gain ratio rho and every gain is net of the static3 prompt (Measurement C: expert k3 - static3 = +17.2). Tests are paired net-point contrasts at 6 seeds (+/-4.6 net) with margins stated as fractions of the +17.2 Gate-0 effect. We predict that lowering agreement at fixed capability leaves the gain within +/-7 net while raising capability at matched agreement adds >= 4; that count-matched foreign pools beat the reader's own pool by >= 6 exactly where kappa >= 0.08 and not where kappa <= 0.02, including mutual gain between two equally capable backbones with different type profiles; and, in a three-arm triple at identical per-type count, that expert solutions to the games the reader fails beat expert solutions to games the reader solves by >= 6, while the latter are within +/-7 of the reader's own solutions to the same games. A token-matched wrong-type placebo bounds the context-length component. The result is a per-cell rule for when foreign experience is worth reading, stated against the cheapest baselines (static3, own pool at the same cost) and against the archived proximity claim.
Experiments: Setup: ALFWorld, 274 validation games (140 seen / 134 unseen), six task types; readers Q = Qwen3-32B (verified; ReAct, thinking off, T=0) and E = EXAONE-4.0-32B (Gate V: serves in vLLM 0.13 on one A100 and reaches k=0 >= 0.30 at 4 seeds, else dropped). Writers: X expert (on disk); Q-self (on disk); Q-prox: same backbone, candidates T=1.0 same scaffold, T=0.7 Act-first scaffold, T=1.0 paraphrased scaffold, screened on 274 x 1 seed; the chosen candidate has k=0 within +/-3 of Q-self and pi(Q-prox,Q) at least 0.10 below pi(Q-self,Q) and closest to pi(Q-cap,Q) (fallback: nearest candidate, pi gap reported as covariate); Q-cap: thinking on, thoughts stripped so serialization equals Q-self, must reach k=0 >= Q-self + 12 on 274 x 2 (fallback: the Measurement-B QLoRA writer); E-self; G-self (gpt-oss-120b; Gate V-G: serves and collects at success >= 0.30, else dropped). Every backbone writer runs the same 3,553 training games once (matched episode budget; GPU-hours reported). Bank construction, identical for all pools: success filter; then per type t draw n_R(t) items at random (one fixed seed) where n_R(t) is the reader's own success count on t; a writer with fewer than n_R(t) successes on t contributes all of them and the deficit is filled with the reader's own items (fill fraction reported; a cell with fill > 10% gets its own self subsample R_match as comparator, reserve two cells = 3,288 episodes). Same retriever (task-description embedding, type-agnostic cosine), same injection template (reader's scaffold), k=3 throughout (the largest static residual, +17.2). Offline statistics before any transfer cell: pi(W,R) on 300 stratified states per pool (~1 GPU-hour); kappa(W,R) from the writer's per-type success on the collection run and the reader's k=0 per-type validation success (Q: existing runs plus 2 seeds to reach >= 4; E: 4 seeds, ~180 episodes per type); each cross cell is classed high (kappa >= 0.08), low (<= 0.02) or unclassed and the table is frozen. Cells (274 games x seeds): reader Q: static3 x6 (4 new), Q-self x6, Q-prox_m x6, Q-cap_m x6, X_m x6, E_m x6, G_m x6, triple self_int / X_int / X_comp x6 each (per type n(t) = min(n_R(t), reader failure count on t); self_int = the reader's own trajectories on a random subset G_t of its solved games, X_int = expert trajectories on the same G_t, X_comp = expert trajectories on an equal-size random subset of the reader's failed games of type t), blind3 placebo x6 (wrong-type items at the k=3 token count), X natural on disk x2 (coverage ablation): 11 new cells = 17,536 episodes (+548 k0). Reader E: k0 x4, static3 x6, E-self x6, X_m x6, Q-self_m x6, G_m x6 = 9,316. Collection: 4 writers x 3,553 = 14,212, screens ~1,400. Total ~43,000 episodes (1.8x the previous plan's 24,000 at ~3 days), about 5-6 days: GPU1 collects Q-cap, Q-prox, E-self, G-self while GPU0 serves reader Q; then both GPUs serve readers with clients spread across replicas; Gate V failures shrink it (no E: -14,500; no G: -6,800). Analysis: paired game x seed contrasts with cluster bootstrap CIs (2,000 resamples); rho per cell with CI; P2 cell-level tests plus a Fisher exact 2x2 (kappa class x outcome) over the 8 cross cells; per-type and seen/unseen breakdowns descriptive. Pre-registration of Gate V, manipulation checks, the frozen kappa table, margins and the cell list before the first confirmatory cell.
Baselines and Ablations: k=0 per reader; static3 (Measurement C: 3 fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, ~430 tokens) per reader, every gain reported net of it; the reader's own success-filtered pool at matched episode budget (denominator of rho and comparator of every Delta); count-matched vs natural expert pool for reader Q (coverage component of the natural rho(X->Q), whose numerator Measurement C already puts at +17.2 over static3); the self_int / X_int / X_comp triple (single-factor contrasts: writer identity at identical games and count, and game subset at identical writer and count); blind3 token-matched wrong-type placebo for reader Q (context-length bound; Measurement C's blind1 is -3 under k0 at k=1); manipulation-check cells reported in their own right (Q-prox k=0 and pi; Q-cap k=0 and pi); writer-denominator ratio rho_w for the Q<->E pair (Q-self_m->E over Q-self->Q, E_m->Q over E-self->E); R_match self subsample for any cell with fill > 10%; a second 2x2 with the writer's overall k=0 advantage as classifier, the competing predictor; seen vs unseen and per-type gains descriptive. Removed because they carried no claim at this budget: k=1 arms, the hierarchical-memory reimplementation, the mixed pool, reader G, and the length-filtered self-opt/self-rand pair (replaced by the triple, which varies one factor at a time).
Falsifiable Predictions:
All contrasts are paired over 274 games x 6 seeds (95% half-width +/-4.6 net, 90% +/-3.9); margins are fractions of the +17.2 Gate-0 effect; each falsifier is at least one half-width from its prediction.
P1 (proximity inert, capability not; reader Q). (a) Delta_prox = S(Q-prox_m) - S(Q-self) lies in the equivalence band [-7, +7] (TOST: 90% CI inside the band). Falsified if Delta_prox <= -8 with 95% CI excluding 0, the closer_beats_stronger direction; produced by the Q-prox_m cell, whose items are verified to agree with the reader's greedy action at least 0.10 less often than Q-self's. (b) At matched agreement (pi(Q-cap) within 0.05 of pi(Q-prox)), Delta_cap = S(Q-cap_m) - S(Q-prox_m) >= +4 (0.25 of Gate 0, consistent with kappa(Q-cap,Q) being about a quarter of kappa(X,Q)). Falsified if Delta_cap <= -1 (95% CI then excludes +4); produced by the Q-cap_m cell, which sits on Q-self's type histogram and differs only by containing games Q-self fails; a null means static3's procedure hint is all a stronger same-family writer adds. Also falsified, in favour of a same-family proximity advantage, if Delta_cap >= Delta_m(X_m->Q) + 5.
P2 (headline; which cells beat the reader's own pool). For each cross cell, Delta_m(W->R) = S_R(W_m) - S_R(R-self), W_m on the reader's own type histogram. Predicted: every high-kappa cell (>= 0.08) has Delta_m >= +6 and every low-kappa cell (<= 0.02) has Delta_m <= +2, classes frozen before the cells run. Falsified by any high-kappa cell with Delta_m <= +1 (CI excludes +6; e.g. X_m->Q if the reader's own successes match expert walkthroughs at equal count, or G_m->Q if a stronger writer's items are unusable by the reader) or any low-kappa cell with Delta_m >= +7 (CI excludes +2; e.g. Q-prox_m->Q if diverse same-capability successes help; this cell is shared with P1a, so the low side is independently informative only through other-backbone cells). Sub-prediction for the equal-capability pair: if kappa(E,Q) and kappa(Q,E) are both >= 0.08 (profiles differ) then Delta_m(E->Q) and Delta_m(Q->E) are both >= +6 although neither writer is stronger overall; if both <= 0.02 then both <= +2; falsified by an asymmetric outcome in which only the stronger-overall writer's pool helps. Secondary: Fisher exact 2x2 (kappa class x outcome) over the 8 cross cells, and the same 2x2 with overall k=0 advantage as classifier; where the two disagree, kappa is predicted right.
P3 (where the gain comes from; reader Q, identical writer and count). Delta_comp = S(X_comp) - S(X_int) >= +6: expert solutions to the games the reader fails beat expert solutions to games the reader solves. Falsified if Delta_comp <= +1 (CI excludes +6), meaning the expert's value is optimality or format available on any game; produced by the triple.
P4 (optimality null; reader Q, identical games). Delta_opt = S(X_int) - S(self_int) lies in [-7, +7] (TOST): expert walkthroughs of games the reader already solves are worth no more than the reader's own solutions of the same games. Falsified if Delta_opt >= +8 with CI excluding 0; produced by the triple; optimality is then a live channel and P1a is re-read with trajectory length as covariate. P3 and P4 share the X_int arm (a low X_int estimate helps P3 and lowers Delta_opt); both are reported with its CI.
P5 (placebo; reader Q). blind3 - static3 <= +3 with 95% CI upper bound < +8. Falsified if the estimate >= +8 (CI excludes +3): context length alone helps, and every rho is re-based on blind3 instead of static3.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired design: the same 274 games and the same seeds in every cell; 6 seeds for every confirmatory cell, so a paired contrast has 95% half-width about +/-4.6 net (the brief's +/-8 at 2 seeds scaled by sqrt(3)) and 90% about +/-3.9; game x seed cluster bootstrap CIs (2,000 resamples). Tests are stated on paired net-point contrasts, not on rho: with a self-pool denominator of 10-17 net (the expert residual over static3 is +17.2, CI +/-5) rho has a half-width near 0.27 at 6 seeds, so no rho threshold is testable at a feasible seed count; rho is reported per cell with CIs as the brief's estimand and each margin is given in net points as a fraction of the 17.2 Gate-0 effect (+4 = 0.25, +6 = 0.35, +/-7 = 0.4, +8 = 0.45). Each falsifier is at least one half-width from its prediction (+6 vs +1, +4 vs -1, +2 vs +7, -8 vs the +/-7 band); equivalence claims (P1a, P4) are TOSTs with the 90% CI inside +/-7, so a true zero passes when the estimate is within +/-3.1 and an effect of noise-floor size (8) fails. Gate 0 (transfer over the best static arm exists) is already met by Measurement C (+17.2); Gate V (E serves and reaches k=0 >= 0.30; G serves and collects at >= 0.30) precedes collection. Manipulation checks are pre-registered cells: Q-prox k=0 within +/-3 of Q-self, pi lower by >= 0.10 and within 0.05 of pi(Q-cap); Q-cap k=0 >= Q-self + 12; a failed check triggers the named fallback and is reported, never silently substituted. The kappa class table (high >= 0.08, low <= 0.02) is computed from the collection runs and the readers' k=0 per-type validation success and frozen before any cross cell runs. Multiple comparisons: five pre-registered predictions with cell-level tests; the Fisher 2x2 over 8 cells is a summary, not a gate. Retrieval is identical across readers for a given pool (same embedding, same index); count matching uses one fixed random seed per pool and the fill fraction is reported per type. Throughput (episodes/min, tok/s per GPU) and GPU-hours per pool are logged and reported as collection cost.

(3) closest named method: 'hierarchical memory distilled from large teacher agent trajectories improves small LLM agents without training' (recent) -> 2608.07169 (Agent Memory Distillation, 2 citations), 2607.01224 AutoMem, 2606.02355 SIRI, 2605.17539 MEMOIR, 2602.22406; 2608.07169 remains the closest and has no self-pool control, no proximity measure and one teacher. (4) recent: 'self-generated in-context demonstrations versus demonstrations from other models policy similarity predicts in-context gain' -> no results; retry 'self-generated demonstrations in-context learning other model' -> 2606.26025, 2603.24690, 2511.17839, all irrelevant. No preprint found that predicts transfer from a per-type complementarity statistic, that manipulates proximity at fixed capability, or that separates complement-game from shared-game demonstrations at matched count.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Thinking-on may not raise Qwen3-32B by 12 points; the fallback QLoRA writer changes pi as well, so P1b is then reported against whichever of Q-self / Q-prox matches its pi within 0.05, else with the pi gap as covariate. No Q-prox candidate may land within 0.05 of pi(Q-cap); P1b is then a two-way contrast with pi as covariate. The kappa class table may be degenerate (e.g. only Q-prox_m->Q low, every other cell high); P2 is then decided cell by cell and the 2x2 is uninformative, which is why cell-level margins are the test. Count matching discards items for strong writers (the expert pool loses roughly 40-50% of its items), so the matched rho understates the natural rho; the natural X->Q cell reports the coverage component at 2 seeds (+/-8). Writers weaker than the reader on a type have their matched pool filled with the reader's own items; cells with fill > 10% get an R_match comparator (reserve 3,288 episodes). EXAONE-4.0-32B and gpt-oss-120b are unverified in vLLM 0.13 (gpt-oss MXFP4 on A100 runs through a fallback kernel and may take 12-16 GPU-hours for 3,553 games); Gate V failures shrink P2 to 5 or 6 cross cells and remove the mutual-gain sub-prediction. If reader E is near ceiling its failure set is small and kappa(W,E) is near zero for every writer; E then only tests the low-kappa side. The triple's per-type count is limited by the reader's failure count on ceiling types (about 60 games), so retrieval density is lower in the triple than in the matched cells; its contrasts are internal and unaffected. ALFWorld has six coarse types, so complementarity has few degrees of freedom and the result may be specific to procedure-bound domains; a WebShop replication is follow-up. Matched cost is defined by episode budget; GPU-hours differ by backbone and are reported. At ~43,000 episodes the study is 1.8x the previous plan and takes 5-6 days with both GPUs busy; that is the price of margins outside the noise.
Addresses gap: G3 (size and direction of the capability gap and family mismatch, with proximity and capability separated by manipulation rather than observed) and G1 (retained-gain ratio per writer x reader cell, with a count-matched variant that isolates content from coverage), with G2's matched-cost self-pool control built into the estimand.
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: Measurement A (expert -> Qwen3-32B, k3 - static3 = +17.2, gain carried by clean/heat/cool). This idea claims that the same per-type profile, turned into a writer-reader statistic kappa, predicts every writer x reader cell at matched item count, including which foreign pools beat the reader's own matched-cost pool and which subset of the expert's games carries the gain; Measurement A cannot say this with one writer, no self-pool arm and no game-level split. Nearest digest card: arXiv:2608.07169 (teacher effectiveness 'depends on teacher capability and student compatibility'). This idea separates capability into measured per-type complementarity and compatibility into measured action agreement, manipulates each at a fixed level of the other, and reports the ratio against the student's own pool at matched cost and count, none of which the card does. Archived closer_beats_stronger predicted proximity; this idea predicts proximity is inert at fixed serialization, with proximity manipulated at fixed capability and capability at matched proximity, the separation the judges asked for, and adds a claim neither made: an expert's optimal solutions to games the reader already solves transfer nothing beyond the reader's own.
Changes made: P1: rho thresholds replaced by net-point margins as fractions of the +17.2 Gate-0 effect (a 10-17 net denominator makes rho untestable); 6 seeds (+/-4.6); proximity half is a TOST with band +/-7; capability half is now Q-cap vs Q-prox at matched pi (capability at fixed proximity, as the brief requires), +4 vs -1; reader E dropped from P1. P2 (headline): every foreign pool subsampled to the reader's own per-type item count, breaking the kappa-coverage identity; cell-level tests (+6 vs +1, +2 vs +7) on a frozen kappa class table; Spearman thresholds dropped, Fisher 2x2 kept as summary; mutual-gain sub-prediction for the equal-capability E<->Q pair and the overall-capability classifier as competing predictor added. P3: the share-of-gain test (forced by headroom) replaced by a game-level arm, X_comp vs X_int at identical writer and count, so the falsifier is reachable. P4: self-opt/self-rand (two factors) replaced by X_int vs self_int, varying only who wrote the trajectory at identical games; direction reversed to an equivalence prediction, the risky one under the hypothesis. P5: placebo raised to 6 seeds and stated as a bound (<= +3, CI upper < +8) with a pre-registered re-basing rule. Kept sharp: the claim now says foreign experience is worth reading only for the writer's solutions to the reader's failures and that an expert's optimal solutions to games the reader already solves are worth nothing beyond the reader's own, which is stronger than the previous version, not a hedge. Cut: k=1 arms, hierarchical-memory baseline, mixed pool, reader G, Q-prox/Q-cap -> E cells; budget grew to ~43,000 episodes (5-6 days) because open predictions need 6 seeds.
